newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colonia sees higher profits in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colonia sees higher profits in 1996.

text.p: German insurance group Colonia Konzern AG-Colonia Versicherung (CKAG) said on Friday it expected higher profits this year despite a slight fall in premium revenues to 3.28 billion marks.

But this would depend on further developments and the absence of any large damage claims between now and the end of the year, management board chairman Klaus-Dieter Laessker said in a text prepared for delivery at a news conference.
He added that the company's Nordstern Allgemeine unit would achieve premium revenues of 1.55 billion marks, up 0.3 percent from the previous year.
Colonia made a group net profit of 72.8 million marks and Nordstern profits were 82.5 million.
Lassker said he expected the company's damage and liability insurance subsidiaries to grow faster than the market next year. The broader market would see premium revenue growth of around one percent.
